name: A day on Venus is longer than its year

hook_variants.template: On Venus, a day is longer than a year. Math breaks down there.
Which planet has a day longer than its year?
One day on Venus: 243 Earth days. One year: 225. Impossible, right?

sections.text: Venus spins on its axis once every 243 Earth days, but orbits the Sun in 225 Earth days.
So a full day-night cycle takes longer than its entire trip around the Sun.
sections.title: Venus day vs Earth day
sections.label: 1 Venus day = 243 Earth days

sections.text: It also spins backwards. On Venus, the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east.
sections.title: directions

sections.text: Planet scientists think a giant ancient collision flipped its spin.
sections.title: why
sections.body: a massive impact may have reversed it

sections.text: Surface conditions are hostile: 465°C heat and pressure 92 times Earth's.
sections.subtitle: hot enough to melt lead

sections.text: Follow for more ways planets embarrass Earth.

facts.claim: Venus rotates once every 243 Earth days, a day longer than its 225-day orbital period
Venus rotates retrograde (backwards) so its sun rises in the west
Venus has a 465°C average surface temperature and 92 bar pressure

titles: On Venus, a day is longer than a year
The planet where time makes no sense
